transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
An orreaster is bringing heavy rain and strong winds to parts of the East Coast.
Thousands of people are without power in New Jersey this morning, and roads have flooded
in some shore communities.
National Weather Service meteorologist Frank Pereira says the storm is expected to strengthen
as it moves north this weekend.
"It's going to work its way from the Mid-Atlantic up to around the East of New Jersey south
of Long Island where it's going to kind of sit there for a day or two through the remainder
of the weekend before it finally moves out early next week.
Unfortunately, this system is going to produce some significant coastal flooding."
In the Pacific, Hurricane Nolo is gaining strength and could bring up to 16 inches of
rain to the eastern and southern parts of Hawaii's Big Island.
Off Mexico, Hurricane Polo is now a Category 5 storm.
A hurricane watch has been posted for parts of Baja, California, Sur.
OpenAI says its models probed government websites on their own.
NPR's Shannon Vaughan reports it's the latest episode where AI systems have done things
their developers didn't expect or asked them to do.
OpenAI's AI models tried to hack an Education Department website but were unsuccessful, according
to AI research firm Transloose.
The Education Department said it found no evidence of any impact and OpenAI says it's
reviewing the researcher's findings.
OpenAI has notified dozens of organizations about times its AI acted in what it calls
misaligned ways during training and evaluation.
That includes accessing publicly available Census Bureau data using login keys found
online and copying public information from the Securities and Exchange Commission and
posting it to another website.
The SEC says no non-public information was accessed.
The Census Bureau didn't respond to a request for comment.
Shannon Vaughan, NPR News.
Pope Leo is spending the second day of his visit to France and Paris where he's scheduled
to celebrate an outdoor mass this afternoon and PR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
Fervent crowds screamed Leo's name as they lined the streets of the left bank to get
a glimpse of the pontiff in his Pope Mobile.
Leo also spoke at UNESCO on Friday, the United Nations Education and Cultural Organization
that the U.S. has just left.
He called UNESCO a partner of the church to make the world more just, favoring education
of young people in the face of what he called the paradise of machines.
At Notre Dame, Leo arrived to organ music and cheers.
Speaking in French, he told the crowd of his great joy in being among them in the great
cathedral.
The Pope ended his first day of this visit with a mass with 70,000 young people in the
Paris sports stadium.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
It's NPR.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has listed one death from measles this year
as cases continue to rise across the country.
NPR's Rachel Carlson reports the update comes submitted dispute with Pennsylvania over the
number of deaths linked to the state's outbreak.
The tension stems from public health experts' concerns about the CDC's reliability.
Pennsylvania reported four measles deaths so far in its outbreak in the state.
When the deaths were first reported, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. initially
questioned whether measles was the cause, and the CDC removed them from the agency's
website.
The single death now appearing on the site has an asterisk with a footnote saying the
number is subject to change after more reviews are completed.
It's unclear if this death is from Pennsylvania.
Nationally, there have been over 3,600 measles cases this year.
Rachel Carlson, NPR News.
The Supreme Court has cleared the way for states to use a federal database to check
voters' citizenship ahead of the November midterm elections.
The justices temporarily lifted a lower court decision blocking the Trump administration's
expanded SAFE program.
Voting rights groups warn that errors could wrongly flag eligible voters.
The White House says the system will help states identify non-citizens on their roles.
States can choose whether to use the database.
Federal law also bars most states from carrying out the broad voter roll purges within 90
days of an election.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Nor'easter brings heavy rain and strong winds to East Coast, causing power outages and flooding in New Jersey
Hurricane Nolo strengthens in Pacific, could bring up to 16 inches of rain to Hawaii's Big Island
Hurricane Polo reaches Category 5 strength off Mexico, hurricane watch posted for Baja California Sur
OpenAI AI models probed government websites during training, unsuccessfully attempted to hack Education Department site
Pope Leo celebrates second day of visit to France with outdoor mass in Paris and Notre Dame appearance
CDC lists one measles death this year as cases rise; Pennsylvania reports four deaths in state outbreak
